policy.last_change: 3 Dec 2025 (-25bp, sixth cut of 2025); held 14 Jan 2026

policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 14 Jan close (1x4 3.87, 3x6 3.61, 6x9 3.47, 9x12 3.44 vs WIBOR 3M 3.95) price roughly 50bp of NBP cuts within 12 months. The MPC held all rates on 14 Jan (reference 4.00%). The statement keeps decisions data-dependent, drops energy prices from the list of inflation risks and calls the demand recovery 'expected'. Glapiński speaks on 15 Jan at 15:00. The NBP survey of professional forecasters (2 Jan) sees an average reference rate of 3.69% in 2026. Post-decision views (14 Jan): ING sees the next cut in March with the new projection and at least three cuts in 2026 to 3.25%; Erste expects 25bp in March and another in Q2 to 3.50%; PKO expects March and 3.50% in two quick steps with Q1 CPI near 2%.
policy.risk_text: After the 14 Jan hold the next cut is expected in March with the new projection: a slower path (core CPI ~2.8%, the 'expected' demand recovery) would lift the front end; a quick move to 3.50% (PKO) would extend the rally. Heavy Q1 supply can widen asset swaps (Millennium, 9 Jan).

macro.projection_text: NBP November 2025 projection: CPI 3.7% (2025), 2.9% (2026), 2.5% (2027); December 2025 flash CPI 2.4% y/y.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit ~7.0% of GDP (MoF notified PLN 271bn; 4Q-rolling 7.0% after Q3 per Erste, 12 Jan); the Sejm completed the 2026 budget on 9 Jan (deficit cap PLN 271.7bn, gross borrowing needs ~PLN 690bn); presidential vetoes cost ~PLN 1.8bn in 2026 (Neneman, 9 Jan); budget cash PLN 133.8bn at end-Dec (MoF, 9 Jan). The President may send the budget to the Constitutional Tribunal (no veto right); the government would then run on its draft (Domański, 12 Jan).
macro.fiscal_risk_text: Q1 2026 supply of PLN 75-100bn over 8 auctions: PLN 13.7bn sold on 9 Jan, next 22 Jan (8-13bn) and 28 Jan (7-12bn); MoF is considering JPY, CHF and USD issues (14 Jan); Fitch (27 Feb) and Moody's (20 Mar) reviews with negative outlooks.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP cut six times in 2025 to 4.00% and held on 14 Jan; CPI fell to 2.4% in December (flash, 31 Dec; final on 15 Jan, consensus 2.4% y/y, core ~2.8%), the NBP projects 2.9% for 2026 (professional forecasters, 2 Jan: 2.6%). Manufacturing PMI fell to 48.5 in December (2 Jan). GDP grew 3.8% y/y in Q3. Ratings: Fitch A- negative, Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable. 14 Jan: the MPC held (see policy). Abroad: US retail sales +0.6%, PPI 3.0% y/y; China's December exports +6.6% (3.0% expected); Fed's Kashkari said it is 'way too soon' to cut; Iran strike fears lifted Brent to $66.5 (a three-month high) before Trump's comments eased them; UST 10Y 4.13%, Bund 2.81%; Greenland talks ended in 'fundamental disagreement'. MoF is considering JPY, CHF and USD issues (14 Jan). Street views (December): PKO 1Q26 forecast 2Y 3.75 / 5Y 4.50 / 10Y 5.10 (reached by 7 Jan, PKO); Santander expects higher yields in Q1 on supply and cut repricing; ING says early-2026 trading follows MoF's Q1 issuance.

calendar.plan_text: MoF Q1 2026 financing plan (31 Dec 2025): 8 sale auctions for PLN 75-100bn, one switch auction, possible foreign issuance. January: sale auctions on 9 Jan (PLN 7-12bn), 22 Jan (8-13bn) and 28 Jan (7-12bn); no switch auction in January; 36-week T-bill auction on 16 Jan (PLN 2-4bn). 2026 gross borrowing needs ~PLN 690bn. BGK: FPC to issue domestically in 2026 (up to PLN 18.5bn). MoF priced EUR 3.25bn on 8 Jan (EUR 2bn Jan-2031 at 2.964%, MS+43; EUR 1.25bn Jun-2036 at 3.739%, MS+83). 9 Jan result: PLN 12.0bn sold vs 22.3bn demand (cover 1.86) plus 1.69bn additional sale (DS1035 1.17bn); stop yields OK0128 3.678%, PS0130 4.258%, PS0131 4.504%, DS1033 4.851%, DS1035 5.121%; new NZ0331 PLN 1.26bn at 95.20. Prefinancing at end-2025 was ~21% (final). MoF (12 Jan): 2026 needs ~26% financed. BGK sold PLN 3.73bn of FPC (demand 7.05bn) plus 0.71bn on 12 Jan. The 22 Jan offer had not been published by 14 Jan.
calendar.timing_text: Within each auction week of the Aug 2025-Jan 2026 sample, yields drifted lower into the auction (rally regime) and the auction-day close was the cheapest point relative to the preceding session, so new buying is best executed at the auction-day close (22, 28 Jan) rather than the day before. The 9 Jan auction cleared PLN 13.7bn with 1.86x cover, so supply is being absorbed; 22 and 28 Jan remain (PLN 15-25bn). After the 14 Jan hold the front end is driven by the December final CPI (15 Jan, 10:00), Glapiński's press conference (15 Jan, 15:00) and the March projection.

facts.core_text: Regime: the NBP paused at 4.00% and held again on 14 Jan with ~50bp more priced, the ECB is done at 2.00%, the Fed and BoE are easing gradually, the CNB and MNB are on hold. Poland's 5Y CDS was 60bp and the 10Y spread to Bunds 231bp on benchmark bonds (Erste, 14 Jan close; ~10bp less here on DS1035 vs the Bundesbank fitted 10Y). Iran risk lifted Brent to $66.5 on 14 Jan; UST 10Y 4.13%, Bund 2.81%.

quasi_takeaways: FPC fixed lines trade ~{lo}-{hi}bp over the POLGB curve (average {avg}bp); widest ASW {widest} at {widest_asw}bp. Same State Treasury guarantee as POLGBs.
Best pickup: {best} ({best_sp}bp vs POLGB). For buy-and-hold books the guarantee makes the pickup attractive; liquidity is the cost (Pekao became BGK market maker on 13 Nov 2025).

12 Jan BGK auction: PLN 3.73bn sold against 7.05bn demand, plus 0.71bn in the additional sale (~PLN 4.4bn, about a quarter of the 2026 FPC plan of up to 18.5bn); per-series levels were not found. The 1.9x cover shows real-money demand for guaranteed paper at these spreads.
Use auctions, not Catalyst: trades are small retail lots and some lines go weeks without a print.
